variants.definition: ảnh hưởng của thương hiệu đến nhận thức, lựa chọn tiêu dùng
variants.example: Brand influence can lead consumers to pay more for familiar products even when cheaper alternatives offer comparable quality.

originalRelations.synonyms: impact · leverage · sway · social influence · agenda-setting power
originalRelations.antonyms: powerlessness · limited impact · lack of leverage · marginal influence · irrelevance

variants.originalDefinition: ảnh hưởng thương hiệu
variants.originalExample: One reason brand influence matters is that it shapes not only average outcomes but also how opportunities and risks are distributed across social groups.

cards.originalDefinition: ảnh hưởng thương hiệu

cards.definition: đòn bẩy; lợi thế, sức tác động để đạt mục tiêu
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: đòn bẩy; lợi thế, sức tác động để đạt mục tiêu
variants.example: A major employer may use its commercial leverage to demand lower prices from suppliers that cannot afford to lose such a large customer.

cards.definition: sức ảnh hưởng
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: sức ảnh hưởng
variants.example: Large advertisers may hold considerable sway over a publication if editors fear that critical reporting will lead to the withdrawal of essential revenue.

cards.definition: ảnh hưởng từ quan hệ, nhóm, chuẩn mực xã hội
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: ảnh hưởng từ quan hệ, nhóm, chuẩn mực xã hội
variants.example: Social influence can shape purchasing decisions when people choose products to fit in with their peers.
variants.originalDefinition: ảnh hưởng xã hội
variants.originalExample: Governments that prioritise social influence can improve informed consumer choice and market transparency, provided that implementation is transparent and responsive to evidence.

cards.originalDefinition: ảnh hưởng xã hội

cards.definition: khả năng định hướng vấn đề được chú ý, thảo luận, ưu tiên
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: khả năng định hướng vấn đề được chú ý, thảo luận, ưu tiên
variants.example: Large news organisations exercise agenda-setting power by deciding which issues receive sustained coverage.
variants.originalDefinition: quyền lực định hình chương trình nghị sự
variants.originalExample: Weak agenda-setting power can impose diffuse costs that are easy to ignore initially but expensive to correct once manipulation, overconsumption and household waste becomes entrenched.

cards.originalDefinition: quyền lực định hình chương trình nghị sự

cards.definition: sự tự kiềm chế mua sắm
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: sự tự kiềm chế mua sắm
variants.example: Purchasing restraint is easier for me when I wait a day before ordering something that was not on my original shopping list.

originalRelations.synonyms: self-control · moderation · discipline · measured consumption · impulse control
originalRelations.antonyms: excess · indulgence · impulsiveness · overconsumption · lack of control

variants.originalDefinition: sự tiết chế mua sắm
variants.originalExample: An exclusive focus on efficiency can weaken purchasing restraint, which in turn may reduce public confidence even when aggregate performance improves.

cards.originalDefinition: sự tiết chế mua sắm

cards.definition: khả năng tự kiểm soát
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: khả năng tự kiểm soát
variants.example: Self-control can be strengthened by reducing exposure to unnecessary temptations, rather than expecting determination alone to overcome them repeatedly.

cards.definition: sự điều độ
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: sự điều độ
variants.example: Moderation should not be treated as an abstract ideal; it has concrete implications for informed consumer choice and market transparency and for the likelihood of manipulation, overconsumption and household waste.

cards.definition: tính kỷ luật
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: tính kỷ luật
variants.example: Maintaining discipline is easier when classroom rules are predictable and pupils understand how their behaviour affects other people's opportunity to learn.

cards.definition: tiêu dùng có chừng mực và kiểm soát
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: tiêu dùng có chừng mực và kiểm soát
variants.example: Measured consumption involves replacing useful items when necessary rather than buying every new version to maintain an image.
variants.originalDefinition: tiêu dùng có chừng mực
variants.originalExample: If reform strengthens measured consumption only for already advantaged groups, it may widen rather than narrow the underlying problem.

cards.originalDefinition: tiêu dùng có chừng mực

cards.definition: bảo tồn văn hóa
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: bảo tồn văn hóa
variants.example: Cultural preservation is strongest when communities can continue practising their traditions, rather than see them survive only as exhibits for outside audiences.

originalRelations.synonyms: conservation · safeguarding · protection · heritage stewardship · continuity
originalRelations.antonyms: destruction · loss · erosion · neglect · cultural disappearance

variants.originalExample: Cultural preservation deserves serious attention because it can strengthen cultural continuity and creative participation while reducing exposure to cultural erosion and unequal access to the arts.

cards.definition: quản lý, gìn giữ di sản có trách nhiệm
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: quản lý, gìn giữ di sản có trách nhiệm
variants.example: Heritage stewardship requires regular maintenance of historic buildings, not simply a restoration campaign after serious damage has occurred.
variants.originalDefinition: trách nhiệm gìn giữ di sản
variants.originalExample: The value of heritage stewardship should be judged by its real-world effects on cultural continuity and creative participation, not merely by whether it sounds politically attractive.

cards.originalDefinition: trách nhiệm gìn giữ di sản

cards.definition: tính liên tục, không gián đoạn
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: tính liên tục, không gián đoạn
variants.example: Where continuity is weak, governments often face higher long-term costs because cultural erosion and unequal access to the arts becomes harder to reverse.

variants.definition: tính liên tục, không gián đoạn
variants.example: Investment in continuity is difficult to justify if it produces impressive headline figures while leaving early disadvantage and long-term developmental harm largely untouched.

cards.definition: khả năng tiếp cận dành cho công chúng
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: khả năng tiếp cận dành cho công chúng
variants.example: Public access to a collection is limited in practice when inconvenient opening hours exclude the people the institution claims to serve.

originalRelations.synonyms: open access · universal availability · public availability · barrier-free entry · broad civic access
originalRelations.antonyms: restricted entry · exclusion · limited access · privatisation of access · access barriers

variants.originalDefinition: khả năng tiếp cận công chúng
variants.originalExample: A well-designed policy can strengthen public access, but its success ultimately depends on whether the gains persist once temporary funding or political attention fades.

cards.originalDefinition: khả năng tiếp cận công chúng

cards.definition: tiếp cận tự do tài liệu, nguồn thông tin
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: tiếp cận tự do tài liệu, nguồn thông tin
variants.example: Open access to cultural resources can widen participation, provided that digitisation is accompanied by formats people can actually use.
variants.originalExample: Debate about open access is often oversimplified; the more useful question is which institutional conditions allow it to improve cultural continuity and creative participation in practice.

variants.definition: tiếp cận tự do tài liệu, nguồn thông tin
variants.example: Open access to cultural resources can widen participation, provided that digitisation is accompanied by formats people can actually use.
variants.originalExample: A failure to secure open access can quietly intensify structural discrimination and exclusion, even when headline indicators initially appear positive.

cards.definition: sự sẵn có của hàng hóa, dịch vụ, cơ hội cho mọi người
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: sự sẵn có của hàng hóa, dịch vụ, cơ hội cho mọi người
variants.example: Universal availability of a service requires more than placing it online if some residents lack internet access or digital skills.
variants.originalDefinition: mức độ sẵn có cho mọi người
variants.originalExample: Investment in universal availability is difficult to justify if it produces impressive headline figures while leaving cultural erosion and unequal access to the arts largely untouched.

cards.originalDefinition: mức độ sẵn có cho mọi người

cards.definition: mức độ sẵn có cho công chúng sử dụng
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: mức độ sẵn có cho công chúng sử dụng
variants.example: Public availability of inspection reports allows residents to examine how safety rules are enforced.
variants.originalDefinition: mức độ sẵn có cho công chúng
variants.originalExample: Public availability should therefore be assessed through longitudinal evidence, particularly where benefits and costs emerge at different points in time.

cards.originalDefinition: mức độ sẵn có cho công chúng

cards.definition: lối vào, tiếp cận không rào cản, kể cả với người khuyết tật
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: lối vào, tiếp cận không rào cản, kể cả với người khuyết tật
variants.example: Barrier-free entry to the gallery requires more than a ramp if visitors still encounter narrow doors and inaccessible ticket machines.
variants.originalDefinition: khả năng tiếp cận không rào cản
variants.originalExample: When authorities neglect barrier-free entry, apparently minor weaknesses can accumulate until they begin to undermine cultural continuity and creative participation.

cards.originalDefinition: khả năng tiếp cận không rào cản

cards.definition: khả năng tiếp cận rộng rãi của công chúng
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: khả năng tiếp cận rộng rãi của công chúng
variants.example: Broad civic access requires cultural institutions to reach beyond their existing audiences rather than assume that opening a door creates equal opportunity.
variants.originalExample: Strengthening broad civic access may involve upfront costs, yet those costs can be outweighed by the long-term damage associated with cultural erosion and unequal access to the arts.

cards.definition: tham gia hoạt động văn hóa
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: tham gia hoạt động văn hóa
variants.example: Libraries can widen cultural participation by hosting affordable workshops and making local performances accessible to residents with disabilities.

originalRelations.synonyms: engagement · involvement · civic participation · active involvement · public input
originalRelations.antonyms: disengagement · non-participation · exclusion · apathy · withdrawal

variants.originalDefinition: sự tham gia văn hóa
variants.originalExample: One reason cultural participation matters is that it shapes not only average outcomes but also how opportunities and risks are distributed across social groups.

cards.originalDefinition: sự tham gia văn hóa

cards.definition: mức độ tham gia
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: mức độ tham gia
variants.example: Public engagement is more credible when residents can influence a planning decision, rather than merely attend a consultation after the main choices have been made.
variants.originalExample: The practical significance of engagement becomes clearer when policy is evaluated at household, community and institutional levels rather than through national averages alone.

cards.definition: sự tham gia
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: sự tham gia
variants.example: Parental involvement is valuable when it supports a child's growing independence rather than turning every school assignment into a measure of family status.

cards.definition: sự tham gia tích cực hoặc chủ động
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: sự tham gia tích cực hoặc chủ động
variants.example: Active involvement in local festivals allows residents to shape the programme instead of remaining passive spectators.
variants.originalDefinition: sự tham gia chủ động
variants.originalExample: Governments that prioritise active involvement can improve cultural continuity and creative participation, provided that implementation is transparent and responsive to evidence.

cards.originalDefinition: sự tham gia chủ động

cards.definition: ý kiến, đề xuất của công chúng
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: ý kiến, đề xuất của công chúng
variants.example: Public input led the planners to move the bus stop closer to the clinic, where many elderly residents needed it.
variants.originalDefinition: ý kiến đóng góp của công chúng
variants.originalExample: Weak public input can impose diffuse costs that are easy to ignore initially but expensive to correct once cultural erosion and unequal access to the arts becomes entrenched.

cards.originalDefinition: ý kiến đóng góp của công chúng

cards.definition: đa dạng cách sáng tạo, thể hiện và tác phẩm
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: đa dạng cách sáng tạo, thể hiện và tác phẩm
variants.example: Supporting small publishers can increase creative diversity by giving unconventional writers a route to readers.

originalRelations.synonyms: pluralism · variety · heterogeneity · cultural plurality · broad representation
originalRelations.antonyms: homogeneity · uniformity · monoculture · narrow representation · cultural conformity

variants.originalDefinition: đa dạng sáng tạo
variants.originalExample: An exclusive focus on efficiency can weaken creative diversity, which in turn may reduce public confidence even when aggregate performance improves.

cards.originalDefinition: đa dạng sáng tạo

cards.definition: sự trung thực, tuân thủ đạo đức nghiên cứu
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: sự trung thực, tuân thủ đạo đức nghiên cứu
variants.example: Research integrity requires authors to report inconvenient results rather than removing observations that weaken their argument.

originalRelations.synonyms: ethical reliability · honesty · research ethics · methodological soundness · professional integrity
originalRelations.antonyms: misconduct · fabrication · bias · ethical breach · corruption

variants.originalDefinition: liêm chính nghiên cứu
variants.originalExample: Research integrity deserves serious attention because it can strengthen credible innovation and evidence-based decision-making while reducing exposure to research waste, ethical failure and public mistrust.

cards.originalDefinition: liêm chính nghiên cứu

cards.definition: độ tin cậy trong tuân thủ đạo đức
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: độ tin cậy trong tuân thủ đạo đức
variants.example: Ethical reliability is demonstrated when a professional applies the same principles even when doing so offers no personal advantage.
variants.originalDefinition: độ đáng tin về mặt đạo đức
variants.originalExample: In debates about science, research & space, ethical reliability matters less as a slogan than as a mechanism capable of changing who benefits, who pays and what happens over time.

cards.originalDefinition: độ đáng tin về mặt đạo đức

cards.definition: tính trung thực
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: tính trung thực
variants.example: Policies that improve honesty are most defensible when they produce measurable gains in credible innovation and evidence-based decision-making without shifting hidden costs onto vulnerable groups.

cards.definition: tính hợp lý, đáng tin cậy của phương pháp
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: tính hợp lý, đáng tin cậy của phương pháp
variants.example: Methodological soundness depends on whether a study's design can answer its question, not on how sophisticated its statistical software appears.
variants.originalDefinition: độ vững chắc về phương pháp
variants.originalExample: The value of methodological soundness should be judged by its real-world effects on credible innovation and evidence-based decision-making, not merely by whether it sounds politically attractive.

cards.originalDefinition: độ vững chắc về phương pháp

cards.definition: sự trung thực, tuân thủ đạo đức nghề nghiệp
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: sự trung thực, tuân thủ đạo đức nghề nghiệp
variants.example: Professional integrity requires a researcher to report inconvenient results rather than selecting only the findings that support a sponsor's preferred conclusion.
variants.originalDefinition: liêm chính nghề nghiệp
variants.originalExample: Where professional integrity is weak, governments often face higher long-term costs because research waste, ethical failure and public mistrust becomes harder to reverse.

cards.originalDefinition: liêm chính nghề nghiệp

cards.definition: năng lực đổi mới
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: năng lực đổi mới
variants.example: Innovation capacity depends on the ability to turn ideas into workable improvements, not simply the amount spent on research.

originalRelations.synonyms: capability · institutional capability · productive potential · ability to deliver · operational strength
originalRelations.antonyms: limited capability · capacity constraint · institutional weakness · bottleneck · under-capacity

variants.originalExample: A well-designed policy can strengthen innovation capacity, but its success ultimately depends on whether the gains persist once temporary funding or political attention fades.

cards.definition: giám sát việc tuân thủ đạo đức
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: giám sát việc tuân thủ đạo đức
variants.example: Ethical oversight should require researchers to explain how participants' consent and personal data will be protected.

originalRelations.synonyms: scrutiny · supervision · monitoring · regulatory review · institutional checks
originalRelations.antonyms: neglect · weak supervision · regulatory capture · absence of scrutiny · unchecked discretion

variants.originalDefinition: giám sát đạo đức
variants.originalExample: One reason ethical oversight matters is that it shapes not only average outcomes but also how opportunities and risks are distributed across social groups.

cards.originalDefinition: giám sát đạo đức

cards.definition: sự xem xét kỹ lưỡng
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: sự xem xét kỹ lưỡng
variants.example: The developer's environmental assessment deserves close scrutiny because several of its assumptions have not been supported by independent measurements.

cards.definition: sự giám sát trực tiếp
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: sự giám sát trực tiếp
variants.example: Novice laboratory staff need appropriate supervision until they can recognise hazards and perform unfamiliar procedures without placing colleagues at risk.

cards.definition: việc giám sát
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: việc giám sát
variants.example: Continuous monitoring of the reservoir can reveal a developing leak before the loss of water becomes visible to nearby residents.

cards.definition: rà soát quy định, vấn đề quản lý nhà nước
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: rà soát quy định, vấn đề quản lý nhà nước
variants.example: A regulatory review can reveal whether an outdated licensing requirement still protects the public or merely delays small businesses.
variants.originalDefinition: việc rà soát quy định
variants.originalExample: Governments that prioritise regulatory review can improve credible innovation and evidence-based decision-making, provided that implementation is transparent and responsive to evidence.

cards.originalDefinition: việc rà soát quy định

cards.definition: cơ chế kiểm soát quyền lực, ngăn lạm dụng trong thể chế
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: cơ chế kiểm soát quyền lực, ngăn lạm dụng trong thể chế
variants.example: Institutional checks, such as independent audits, can prevent officials from approving contracts in which they have a personal interest.
variants.originalDefinition: các cơ chế kiểm soát thể chế
variants.originalExample: Weak institutional checks can impose diffuse costs that are easy to ignore initially but expensive to correct once research waste, ethical failure and public mistrust becomes entrenched.

cards.originalDefinition: các cơ chế kiểm soát thể chế

cards.definition: kinh phí công cho nghiên cứu
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: kinh phí công cho nghiên cứu
variants.example: Public research funding can support long-term investigations that offer substantial social value but little immediate commercial return.

originalRelations.synonyms: financing · public investment · budget allocation · financial support · resource commitment
originalRelations.antonyms: underfunding · budget cuts · financial shortfall · disinvestment · funding gap

variants.originalDefinition: tài trợ công cho nghiên cứu
variants.originalExample: An exclusive focus on efficiency can weaken public research funding, which in turn may reduce public confidence even when aggregate performance improves.

cards.originalDefinition: tài trợ công cho nghiên cứu

cards.definition: việc cung cấp hoặc huy động vốn
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: việc cung cấp hoặc huy động vốn
variants.example: Reliable financing allows the restoration project to retain skilled staff instead of repeatedly suspending work whenever a short-term grant expires.

cards.definition: phân bổ ngân sách theo khoản chi, đơn vị, mục tiêu
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: phân bổ ngân sách theo khoản chi, đơn vị, mục tiêu
variants.example: Budget allocation should be explained publicly when funding is shifted from preventive maintenance to a more visible construction project.
variants.originalDefinition: phân bổ ngân sách
variants.originalExample: Improving budget allocation requires more than additional funding: it also depends on enforcement, administrative competence and credible accountability.

cards.originalDefinition: phân bổ ngân sách

cards.definition: hỗ trợ tài chính
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: hỗ trợ tài chính
variants.example: Financial support should reflect the recipient’s actual needs; a payment that looks generous on paper may still be inadequate where essential costs are high.
variants.originalExample: If reform strengthens financial support only for already advantaged groups, it may widen rather than narrow the underlying problem.

cards.definition: cam kết dành nguồn lực cho mục tiêu
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: cam kết dành nguồn lực cho mục tiêu
variants.example: A government's resource commitment is credible only when the announced programme has a realistic budget and enough trained staff to deliver it.
variants.originalDefinition: cam kết nguồn lực
variants.originalExample: A balanced approach to resource commitment should recognise legitimate trade-offs while still protecting the institutional foundations of credible innovation and evidence-based decision-making.

cards.originalDefinition: cam kết nguồn lực

cards.definition: sức khỏe, an toàn và cuộc sống tốt của trẻ
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: sức khỏe, an toàn và cuộc sống tốt của trẻ
variants.example: Child well-being depends on stable care and a safe environment as well as access to education and healthcare.

originalRelations.synonyms: welfare · quality of life · psychological health · life satisfaction · personal flourishing
originalRelations.antonyms: distress · poor mental health · low quality of life · burnout · psychological strain

variants.originalDefinition: phúc lợi trẻ em
variants.originalExample: Child well-being deserves serious attention because it can strengthen healthy development and stable family relationships while reducing exposure to early disadvantage and long-term developmental harm.

cards.originalDefinition: phúc lợi trẻ em

cards.definition: trách nhiệm, nghĩa vụ của cha mẹ với con
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: trách nhiệm, nghĩa vụ của cha mẹ với con
variants.example: Parental responsibility includes setting reasonable boundaries while listening to a child's concerns.

originalRelations.synonyms: duty · accountability · obligation · parental stewardship · responsible conduct
originalRelations.antonyms: neglect · irresponsibility · abdication of duty · carelessness · lack of accountability

variants.originalDefinition: trách nhiệm của cha mẹ
variants.originalExample: Improving parental responsibility can be a high-leverage intervention when it addresses structural constraints rather than treating only visible symptoms.

cards.originalDefinition: trách nhiệm của cha mẹ

cards.definition: nghĩa vụ
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: nghĩa vụ
variants.example: A landlord has a duty to address dangerous electrical faults promptly, even when arranging repairs is inconvenient or financially unwelcome.

cards.definition: trách nhiệm giải trình, chịu trách nhiệm về việc mình làm
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: trách nhiệm giải trình, chịu trách nhiệm về việc mình làm
variants.example: Accountability is weakened when officials can approve a costly project without explaining its objectives or accepting responsibility for its failure.

cards.definition: nghĩa vụ
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: nghĩa vụ
variants.example: The strongest case for obligation rests on evidence that it improves healthy development and stable family relationships rather than merely redistributing problems from one group to another.

cards.definition: trách nhiệm chăm sóc, bảo vệ và định hướng của cha mẹ
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: trách nhiệm chăm sóc, bảo vệ và định hướng của cha mẹ
variants.example: Parental stewardship involves setting reasonable boundaries while gradually allowing children to make decisions for themselves.
variants.originalDefinition: trách nhiệm định hướng và chăm sóc của cha mẹ
variants.originalExample: Policymakers should treat parental stewardship as part of a wider system, since isolated interventions rarely eliminate the structural drivers of early disadvantage and long-term developmental harm.

cards.originalDefinition: trách nhiệm định hướng và chăm sóc của cha mẹ

cards.definition: hành vi có trách nhiệm, cân nhắc hậu quả
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: hành vi có trách nhiệm, cân nhắc hậu quả
variants.example: Responsible conduct includes admitting a mistake promptly and helping to repair the harm it has caused.
variants.originalDefinition: hành vi có trách nhiệm
variants.originalExample: Responsible conduct becomes especially important when short-term efficiency conflicts with fairness, resilience or long-term institutional credibility.

cards.originalDefinition: hành vi có trách nhiệm

cards.definition: sự ổn định, nhất quán trong gia đình
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: sự ổn định, nhất quán trong gia đình
variants.example: Family stability can be strengthened by predictable working hours that allow parents to organise childcare consistently.

originalRelations.synonyms: security · continuity · predictability · family cohesion · long-term steadiness
originalRelations.antonyms: instability · disruption · uncertainty · breakdown · volatility

variants.originalDefinition: sự ổn định gia đình
variants.originalExample: A well-designed policy can strengthen family stability, but its success ultimately depends on whether the gains persist once temporary funding or political attention fades.

cards.originalDefinition: sự ổn định gia đình

cards.definition: sự ổn định lâu dài
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: sự ổn định lâu dài
variants.example: Long-term steadiness in family routines can give children a sense of security, even when occasional changes are unavoidable.
variants.originalDefinition: sự ổn định dài hạn
variants.originalExample: Strengthening long-term steadiness may involve upfront costs, yet those costs can be outweighed by the long-term damage associated with early disadvantage and long-term developmental harm.

cards.originalDefinition: sự ổn định dài hạn

cards.definition: sự phát triển đầu đời của trẻ
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: sự phát triển đầu đời của trẻ
variants.example: Consistent interaction with caregivers supports early development by giving young children opportunities to practise language and explore their surroundings.

originalRelations.synonyms: advancement · progress · capacity building · growth · maturation
originalRelations.antonyms: stagnation · regression · underdevelopment · decline · developmental setback

variants.originalDefinition: sự phát triển sớm
variants.originalExample: One reason early development matters is that it shapes not only average outcomes but also how opportunities and risks are distributed across social groups.

cards.originalDefinition: sự phát triển sớm

cards.definition: sự tiến bộ / phát triển
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: sự tiến bộ / phát triển
variants.example: Career advancement should depend on demonstrated competence, rather than an employee's ability to maintain informal connections with senior managers.

cards.definition: sự tiến bộ
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: sự tiến bộ
variants.example: Progress towards reducing homelessness should be measured through stable housing outcomes, rather than the number of temporary beds occupied each night.

cards.definition: nâng cao kỹ năng, nguồn lực và năng lực tổ chức
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: nâng cao kỹ năng, nguồn lực và năng lực tổ chức
variants.example: Capacity building should help local staff manage projects independently rather than leave them dependent on outside consultants.
variants.originalDefinition: nâng cao năng lực
variants.originalExample: Capacity building is most likely to endure when rules, incentives and public expectations reinforce one another instead of pulling in opposite directions.

cards.originalDefinition: nâng cao năng lực

cards.definition: sự tăng trưởng hoặc phát triển
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: sự tăng trưởng hoặc phát triển
variants.example: Governments that prioritise growth can improve healthy development and stable family relationships, provided that implementation is transparent and responsive to evidence.

cards.definition: quá trình trưởng thành / hoàn thiện
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: quá trình trưởng thành / hoàn thiện
variants.example: Weak maturation can impose diffuse costs that are easy to ignore initially but expensive to correct once early disadvantage and long-term developmental harm becomes entrenched.

cards.definition: khả năng tiếp cận dịch vụ chăm trẻ
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: khả năng tiếp cận dịch vụ chăm trẻ
variants.example: Childcare accessibility remains poor when available places are too distant or operate at times that do not match parents’ working hours.

originalRelations.synonyms: universal access · ease of access · availability · reach · barrier-free provision
originalRelations.antonyms: exclusion · inaccessibility · restricted access · service barriers · digital divide

variants.originalExample: An exclusive focus on efficiency can weaken childcare accessibility, which in turn may reduce public confidence even when aggregate performance improves.

cards.definition: cơ hội ngang nhau
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: cơ hội ngang nhau
variants.example: Every applicant should have an equal chance to demonstrate their skills, regardless of whether they can afford expensive interview coaching.
variants.originalDefinition: cơ hội ngang nhau
variants.originalExample: In debates about equality, gender & social justice, equal chance matters less as a slogan than as a mechanism capable of changing who benefits, who pays and what happens over time.

cards.originalDefinition: cơ hội ngang nhau

cards.definition: cơ hội công bằng
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: cơ hội công bằng
variants.example: Fair opportunity requires recruitment criteria that assess relevant ability rather than family connections.
variants.originalDefinition: cơ hội công bằng
variants.originalExample: Policies that improve fair opportunity are most defensible when they produce measurable gains in equal participation and social mobility without shifting hidden costs onto vulnerable groups.

cards.originalDefinition: cơ hội công bằng

cards.definition: tiếp cận, được chọn dựa trên năng lực, thành tích
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: tiếp cận, được chọn dựa trên năng lực, thành tích
variants.example: Merit-based access can be undermined when assessments reward expensive preparation more than the abilities they are intended to measure.
variants.originalExample: Where merit-based access is weak, governments often face higher long-term costs because structural discrimination and exclusion becomes harder to reverse.

cards.definition: bảo đảm mọi nhóm được tham gia và hòa nhập xã hội
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: bảo đảm mọi nhóm được tham gia và hòa nhập xã hội
variants.example: Social inclusion involves removing the practical barriers that prevent people with disabilities from studying, working and taking part in community life.

originalRelations.synonyms: social participation · equal participation · inclusive access · social integration · broad-based participation
originalRelations.antonyms: exclusion · marginalisation · segregation · social isolation · discrimination

variants.originalDefinition: hòa nhập xã hội
variants.originalExample: Improving social inclusion can be a high-leverage intervention when it addresses structural constraints rather than treating only visible symptoms.

cards.originalDefinition: hòa nhập xã hội

cards.definition: chống phân biệt đối xử
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: chống phân biệt đối xử
variants.example: Anti-discrimination policies should address the barriers built into recruitment procedures, as well as overt prejudice against individual applicants.

originalRelations.synonyms: equal treatment · non-discrimination · anti-bias protection · civil-rights protection · equality safeguards
originalRelations.antonyms: discrimination · systemic bias · prejudice · unequal treatment · exclusion

variants.originalExample: One reason anti-discrimination matters is that it shapes not only average outcomes but also how opportunities and risks are distributed across social groups.

cards.definition: bảo vệ khỏi thiên lệch, phân biệt đối xử
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: bảo vệ khỏi thiên lệch, phân biệt đối xử
variants.example: Anti-bias protection requires procedures that make discriminatory decisions easier to identify and challenge, rather than a statement of good intentions alone.
variants.originalExample: Anti-bias protection is most likely to endure when rules, incentives and public expectations reinforce one another instead of pulling in opposite directions.

cards.definition: bảo vệ quyền dân sự
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: bảo vệ quyền dân sự
variants.example: Civil-rights protection is meaningful only when people can challenge unequal treatment without facing prohibitive costs or intimidation.
variants.originalExample: Governments that prioritise civil-rights protection can improve equal participation and social mobility, provided that implementation is transparent and responsive to evidence.

cards.definition: biện pháp bảo đảm bình đẳng
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: biện pháp bảo đảm bình đẳng
variants.example: Equality safeguards should include a clear complaints process so that discrimination can be challenged without fear of retaliation.
variants.originalDefinition: cơ chế bảo đảm bình đẳng
variants.originalExample: Weak equality safeguards can impose diffuse costs that are easy to ignore initially but expensive to correct once structural discrimination and exclusion becomes entrenched.

cards.originalDefinition: cơ chế bảo đảm bình đẳng

cards.definition: công bằng khi phân phối lợi ích, nguồn lực, gánh nặng
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: công bằng khi phân phối lợi ích, nguồn lực, gánh nặng
variants.example: A tax reform should be judged partly by distributive fairness: who gains from it, and who carries the additional burden?

originalRelations.synonyms: procedural justice · impartiality · equitable treatment · due consideration · fair dealing
originalRelations.antonyms: bias · favouritism · discrimination · arbitrariness · unequal treatment

variants.originalDefinition: công bằng phân phối
variants.originalExample: An exclusive focus on efficiency can weaken distributive fairness, which in turn may reduce public confidence even when aggregate performance improves.

cards.originalDefinition: công bằng phân phối

cards.definition: lợi ích kinh tế cho địa phương
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: lợi ích kinh tế cho địa phương
variants.example: A festival creates local economic benefit when visitors spend money with resident-owned businesses rather than only with outside operators.

originalRelations.synonyms: community income gains · local prosperity · regional economic return · community-level economic value · local livelihood gains
originalRelations.antonyms: economic leakage · local economic loss · community displacement · profit extraction · declining local livelihoods

variants.originalDefinition: lợi ích kinh tế địa phương
variants.originalExample: Local economic benefit deserves serious attention because it can strengthen local livelihoods and sustainable destination management while reducing exposure to resident displacement and ecological pressure.

cards.originalDefinition: lợi ích kinh tế địa phương

cards.definition: thu nhập tăng của người dân, tổ chức trong cộng đồng
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: thu nhập tăng của người dân, tổ chức trong cộng đồng
variants.example: Community income gains from tourism are more convincing when local workers and businesses retain a substantial share of visitor spending.
variants.originalDefinition: mức tăng thu nhập cho cộng đồng
variants.originalExample: In debates about tourism & local communities, community income gains matters less as a slogan than as a mechanism capable of changing who benefits, who pays and what happens over time.

cards.originalDefinition: mức tăng thu nhập cho cộng đồng

cards.definition: sự thịnh vượng kinh tế địa phương
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: sự thịnh vượng kinh tế địa phương
variants.example: Tourism contributes to local prosperity when small businesses retain a meaningful share of visitors' spending.
variants.originalDefinition: sự thịnh vượng địa phương
variants.originalExample: Policies that improve local prosperity are most defensible when they produce measurable gains in local livelihoods and sustainable destination management without shifting hidden costs onto vulnerable groups.

cards.originalDefinition: sự thịnh vượng địa phương

cards.definition: lợi ích kinh tế vùng từ hoạt động hoặc đầu tư
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: lợi ích kinh tế vùng từ hoạt động hoặc đầu tư
variants.example: The regional economic return from tourism is greater when hotels buy from nearby farmers instead of importing most of their supplies.
variants.originalDefinition: lợi ích kinh tế cấp vùng
variants.originalExample: A failure to secure regional economic return can quietly intensify resident displacement and ecological pressure, even when headline indicators initially appear positive.

cards.originalDefinition: lợi ích kinh tế cấp vùng

cards.definition: giá trị, lợi ích kinh tế ở cấp cộng đồng
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: giá trị, lợi ích kinh tế ở cấp cộng đồng
variants.example: Community-level economic value from tourism is greater when local businesses supply food and services instead of revenue flowing entirely to outside operators.
variants.originalDefinition: giá trị kinh tế ở cấp cộng đồng
variants.originalExample: The value of community-level economic value should be judged by its real-world effects on local livelihoods and sustainable destination management, not merely by whether it sounds politically attractive.

cards.originalDefinition: giá trị kinh tế ở cấp cộng đồng

cards.definition: cải thiện thu nhập, sinh kế của người dân địa phương
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: cải thiện thu nhập, sinh kế của người dân địa phương
variants.example: Local livelihood gains from tourism are more likely to endure when residents own businesses rather than relying entirely on seasonal casual work.
variants.originalDefinition: lợi ích sinh kế tại địa phương
variants.originalExample: Where local livelihood gains is weak, governments often face higher long-term costs because resident displacement and ecological pressure becomes harder to reverse.

cards.originalDefinition: lợi ích sinh kế tại địa phương

cards.definition: tính chân thực trong biểu hiện, thực hành văn hóa
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: tính chân thực trong biểu hiện, thực hành văn hóa
variants.example: Cultural authenticity can be preserved when performers explain the meaning of a tradition instead of reshaping every detail to meet tourist expectations.

originalRelations.synonyms: genuineness · cultural integrity · local character · originality · faithfulness to tradition
originalRelations.antonyms: commodification · artificiality · staged culture · inauthenticity · cultural dilution

variants.originalDefinition: tính chân thực văn hóa
variants.originalExample: Improving cultural authenticity can be a high-leverage intervention when it addresses structural constraints rather than treating only visible symptoms.

cards.originalDefinition: tính chân thực văn hóa

cards.definition: tính chân thực
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: tính chân thực
variants.example: The genuineness of an apology is difficult to judge when the person offering it continues the behaviour that caused the harm.

cards.definition: sự gìn giữ đặc trưng văn hóa cốt lõi
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: sự gìn giữ đặc trưng văn hóa cốt lõi
variants.example: Tourism initiatives should protect cultural integrity by allowing communities to decide how their ceremonies are presented to visitors.
variants.originalDefinition: tính toàn vẹn văn hóa
variants.originalExample: Cultural integrity can generate broad social value, but only when institutions have the capacity to convert formal commitments into consistent practice.

cards.originalDefinition: tính toàn vẹn văn hóa

cards.definition: nét riêng tạo nên bản sắc địa phương
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: nét riêng tạo nên bản sắc địa phương
variants.example: Renovating old shopfronts can preserve local character without preventing buildings from being used for modern businesses.
variants.originalDefinition: bản sắc địa phương
variants.originalExample: The strongest case for local character rests on evidence that it improves local livelihoods and sustainable destination management rather than merely redistributing problems from one group to another.

cards.originalDefinition: bản sắc địa phương

cards.definition: tính độc đáo về ý tưởng, cách thể hiện
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: tính độc đáo về ý tưởng, cách thể hiện
variants.example: The originality of an artwork lies in how it develops its influences into a distinctive expression, rather than in an unrealistic claim to have no influences at all.
variants.originalExample: Policymakers should treat originality as part of a wider system, since isolated interventions rarely eliminate the structural drivers of resident displacement and ecological pressure.

cards.definition: sự gìn giữ, tuân theo cốt lõi truyền thống
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: sự gìn giữ, tuân theo cốt lõi truyền thống
variants.example: Faithfulness to tradition does not prevent a festival from becoming more accessible, provided that its central practices are respected.
variants.originalDefinition: sự trung thành với truyền thống
variants.originalExample: Faithfulness to tradition becomes especially important when short-term efficiency conflicts with fairness, resilience or long-term institutional credibility.

cards.originalDefinition: sự trung thành với truyền thống

cards.definition: giới hạn số sinh vật, mức sử dụng môi trường duy trì lâu dài
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: giới hạn số sinh vật, mức sử dụng môi trường duy trì lâu dài
variants.example: Environmental carrying capacity can be exceeded when demand for local resources rises faster than ecosystems can replenish them.

originalRelations.synonyms: capability · institutional capability · productive potential · ability to deliver · operational strength
originalRelations.antonyms: limited capability · capacity constraint · institutional weakness · bottleneck · under-capacity

variants.originalDefinition: sức chịu tải môi trường
variants.originalExample: A well-designed policy can strengthen environmental carrying capacity, but its success ultimately depends on whether the gains persist once temporary funding or political attention fades.

cards.originalDefinition: sức chịu tải môi trường

cards.definition: sức khỏe, an toàn, chất lượng sống của cư dân
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: sức khỏe, an toàn, chất lượng sống của cư dân
variants.example: Resident well-being should be considered when approving late-night venues, especially where noise regularly disrupts sleep in nearby homes.

originalRelations.synonyms: welfare · quality of life · psychological health · life satisfaction · personal flourishing
originalRelations.antonyms: distress · poor mental health · low quality of life · burnout · psychological strain

variants.originalDefinition: phúc lợi cư dân
variants.originalExample: One reason resident well-being matters is that it shapes not only average outcomes but also how opportunities and risks are distributed across social groups.

cards.originalDefinition: phúc lợi cư dân

cards.definition: du lịch có trách nhiệm với cộng đồng, môi trường, bên liên quan
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: du lịch có trách nhiệm với cộng đồng, môi trường, bên liên quan
variants.example: Responsible tourism involves respecting local customs and supporting local livelihoods rather than treating a destination as a disposable backdrop.

originalRelations.synonyms: sustainable tourism · ethical travel · community-sensitive tourism · low-impact tourism · responsible travel
originalRelations.antonyms: overtourism · exploitative tourism · mass tourism pressure · irresponsible travel · unsustainable tourism

variants.originalDefinition: du lịch có trách nhiệm
variants.originalExample: An exclusive focus on efficiency can weaken responsible tourism, which in turn may reduce public confidence even when aggregate performance improves.

cards.originalDefinition: du lịch có trách nhiệm

cards.definition: du lịch có đạo đức với con người, động vật, môi trường
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: du lịch có đạo đức với con người, động vật, môi trường
variants.example: Ethical travel includes asking permission before photographing residents and avoiding attractions that exploit animals.
variants.originalDefinition: du lịch có trách nhiệm đạo đức
variants.originalExample: Ethical travel should not be treated as an abstract ideal; it has concrete implications for local livelihoods and sustainable destination management and for the likelihood of resident displacement and ecological pressure.

cards.originalDefinition: du lịch có trách nhiệm đạo đức

cards.definition: du lịch cân nhắc nhu cầu, lợi ích, hoàn cảnh cộng đồng
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: du lịch cân nhắc nhu cầu, lợi ích, hoàn cảnh cộng đồng
variants.example: Community-sensitive tourism consults residents before expanding visitor facilities and responds to concerns about noise, housing and access to shared spaces.
variants.originalDefinition: du lịch tôn trọng lợi ích cộng đồng
variants.originalExample: Improving community-sensitive tourism requires more than additional funding: it also depends on enforcement, administrative competence and credible accountability.

cards.originalDefinition: du lịch tôn trọng lợi ích cộng đồng

cards.definition: du lịch ít hại môi trường, cộng đồng
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: du lịch ít hại môi trường, cộng đồng
variants.example: Low-impact tourism may involve limiting visitor numbers on fragile trails and requiring operators to remove their waste.
variants.originalDefinition: du lịch ít tác động
variants.originalExample: If reform strengthens low-impact tourism only for already advantaged groups, it may widen rather than narrow the underlying problem.

cards.originalDefinition: du lịch ít tác động

cards.definition: chất lượng dinh dưỡng
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: chất lượng dinh dưỡng
variants.example: Nutritional quality should be assessed across a diet as a whole rather than inferred from a single ingredient highlighted on a package.

originalRelations.synonyms: high standards · calibre · excellence · service standard · overall effectiveness
originalRelations.antonyms: poor standards · deterioration · inferior quality · underperformance · substandard provision

variants.originalExample: Improving nutritional quality can be a high-leverage intervention when it addresses structural constraints rather than treating only visible symptoms.

cards.definition: nông nghiệp bền vững về môi trường, sinh kế và xã hội
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: nông nghiệp bền vững về môi trường, sinh kế và xã hội
variants.example: Agricultural sustainability depends on preserving soil and water resources as well as keeping farms economically viable; gains in yield alone provide an incomplete measure of success.

originalRelations.synonyms: long-term viability · sustainable development · ecological durability · resource stewardship · environmental responsibility
originalRelations.antonyms: unsustainability · resource depletion · ecological degradation · short-termism · environmental neglect

variants.originalDefinition: tính bền vững nông nghiệp
variants.originalExample: A well-designed policy can strengthen agricultural sustainability, but its success ultimately depends on whether the gains persist once temporary funding or political attention fades.

cards.originalDefinition: tính bền vững nông nghiệp

cards.definition: khả năng chi trả hàng hóa, dịch vụ của người tiêu dùng
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: khả năng chi trả hàng hóa, dịch vụ của người tiêu dùng
variants.example: Consumer affordability changes with income and essential expenses, so a lower advertised price does not guarantee that a product is within reach.

originalRelations.synonyms: cost accessibility · financial attainability · reasonable pricing · manageable cost · price accessibility
originalRelations.antonyms: prohibitive cost · financial burden · unaffordability · cost barrier · price pressure

variants.originalDefinition: khả năng chi trả của người tiêu dùng
variants.originalExample: One reason consumer affordability matters is that it shapes not only average outcomes but also how opportunities and risks are distributed across social groups.

cards.originalDefinition: khả năng chi trả của người tiêu dùng

cards.definition: khả năng chuỗi cung ứng chống chịu, thích ứng, phục hồi
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: khả năng chuỗi cung ứng chống chịu, thích ứng, phục hồi
variants.example: Supply-chain resilience improves when a manufacturer can switch between qualified suppliers rather than depend on a single source.

originalRelations.synonyms: adaptive capacity · robustness · ability to recover · shock resistance · long-term adaptability
originalRelations.antonyms: vulnerability · fragility · low adaptive capacity · exposure to shocks · systemic weakness

variants.originalDefinition: khả năng chống chịu chuỗi cung ứng
variants.originalExample: An exclusive focus on efficiency can weaken supply-chain resilience, which in turn may reduce public confidence even when aggregate performance improves.

cards.originalDefinition: khả năng chống chịu chuỗi cung ứng

cards.definition: trạng thái khỏe mạnh, thoải mái và sống tốt
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: trạng thái khỏe mạnh, thoải mái và sống tốt
variants.example: In debates about animals, wildlife & biodiversity, well-being matters less as a slogan than as a mechanism capable of changing who benefits, who pays and what happens over time.

cards.definition: đối xử nhân đạo, tránh gây đau khổ không cần thiết
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: đối xử nhân đạo, tránh gây đau khổ không cần thiết
variants.example: Humane treatment of animals requires suitable living conditions and prompt veterinary care, not merely protection from deliberate violence.
variants.originalDefinition: đối xử nhân đạo
variants.originalExample: Policies that improve humane treatment are most defensible when they produce measurable gains in species protection and ecosystem stability without shifting hidden costs onto vulnerable groups.

cards.originalDefinition: đối xử nhân đạo

cards.definition: sự bảo vệ động vật
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: sự bảo vệ động vật
variants.example: Animal protection should address avoidable suffering throughout breeding, transport and care, rather than focus solely on highly publicised rescue cases.
variants.originalExample: A failure to secure animal protection can quietly intensify habitat loss, exploitation and biodiversity collapse, even when headline indicators initially appear positive.

cards.definition: chăm sóc có đạo đức, tôn trọng nhu cầu, tránh gây hại
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: chăm sóc có đạo đức, tôn trọng nhu cầu, tránh gây hại
variants.example: Ethical care of captive wildlife should prioritise appropriate living conditions and expert treatment over opportunities for visitors to take photographs.
variants.originalDefinition: sự chăm sóc có đạo đức
variants.originalExample: Where ethical care is weak, governments often face higher long-term costs because habitat loss, exploitation and biodiversity collapse becomes harder to reverse.

cards.originalDefinition: sự chăm sóc có đạo đức

cards.definition: bảo vệ môi trường sống tự nhiên của các loài
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: bảo vệ môi trường sống tự nhiên của các loài
variants.example: Habitat protection helps conserve the conditions species depend on, which cannot always be restored simply by increasing the number of animals in captivity.

originalRelations.synonyms: safeguarding · conservation · preservation · defence · protective regulation
originalRelations.antonyms: degradation · destruction · exposure · exploitation · neglect

variants.originalExample: Improving habitat protection can be a high-leverage intervention when it addresses structural constraints rather than treating only visible symptoms.

cards.definition: bảo vệ, duy trì sự tồn tại của các loài
cards.label: Writing Task 2

variants.definition: bảo vệ, duy trì sự tồn tại của các loài
